newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 30.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Monday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Market may expect light volume as foreign orders may be capped by the Hong Kong handover and ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting on interest rate policy late this week, Anscor-Hagedorn Securities said in its outlook.

* Sun Hung Kai Securities said the market may be locked in a tight range of 2,750 to 2,850 points but a scheduled reserve requirement cut of one percentage point on July 4 should keep sentiment upbeat.
* Anscor-Hagedorn Securities said end-of-the-month squaring by foreign fund managers may see prices of selected "favourite" stocks rising.
* On Friday, the Philippine composite index closed 2.07 points lower at 2,835.03 points.
* The Dow Jones on Friday ended 33.47 points up at 7,687.72. PLDT's ADR closed down $0/05 at $64 3/4.
* The Philippine peso closed lower at 26.384 vs 26.373 to the dollar.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 15.03125 pct.

* San Miguel Corp said it is reducing beer prices effective June 30 as part of a major shift in business strategy designed to stimulate an industry burdened for the past seven years by high excise taxes, falling volumes and growing price sensitivity.
* Philippine sugar miller Central Azucarera de Tarlac said it has retrenched over 500 workers to survive the slump in the local sugar industry.
* Foreign direct investment in the Philippines rose 6.8 percent in the first quarter of the year to $969 million, the Central Bank said.

* Manila Times said Victorias Milling Co had asked its creditor banks to give it until August to look for an investor that will bail the sugar company out of its financial troubles. The company has sought a moratorium on its principal debt payments.
* Newspaper Philippine Star said the International Monetary Fund has warned of an economic slowdown over the long term if the government would trim down its programmed budget surplus this year.

* The Philippine Star said the Department of Agriculture is pushing for another bidding to sell 51 percent of the Food Terminal Inc after the original bidding failed to attract bidders. - KATHERINE ESPINA 63 2 841-8939 Fax 8176267
